Thanks Mateo — good summary. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive: 

- Security/compliance: we need an outline of available auth modes (token, mTLS, VPC peering) and any evidence of KMS/HSM integration for key storage. Also SOC 2 evidence will be requested by procurement.
- Structured output / tool calling: we need a sample of how Redwood encodes tool schemas and versioning. Is the runtime able to enforce output schemas and reject invalid tool responses?
- Embeddings + reranker: curious about how you handle index updates and reranker re-training latency — we have a 5 minute TTL for near-real-time customer updates.

I uploaded the draft procurement timeline to the shared drive (link below). Wed 10am PT works for our eng/security leads, Ryan will be on the call.

On prompts/governance: please include your recommended prompt versioning scheme and any prompt-injection mitigations (sandboxing, user-intent classification, allow-listing). We run regulated PII workloads in a subset of flows so the governance piece is critical.

Appreciate the attachments — we'll populate the prompt inventory and return it ahead of the call.

—Samira

Samira — quick technical notes ahead of Wed's deep-dive so we can focus the meeting on trade-offs: 

Auth options (short):
- Token-based + customer KMS: simple to onboard; tokens issued by Redwood with per-customer scoping and optional KMS-wrapped keys for model context encryption.
- mTLS + VPC peering: recommended for private deployments or when procurement requires network-level isolation.
- Role-based credentials + short-lived tokens for workers accessing KV cache or embedding upserts.

SDK quickstart / routing:
- SDK provides a Config object (region, model, auth) and a Router policy: latency-first, cost-first, or pinned-model. Router supports failover to a smaller quantized variant automatically.
- We'll demo a sample call that sets structured_output_schema and a tool manifest. Example: order_lookup(schema_v1) — runtime validates tool response vs schema and returns structured error codes if validation fails.

Embeddings + reranker behavior:
- We support batching upserts and near-real-time indexing. For your 5 minute TTL we recommend an ingestion pipeline that writes into a short-lived hot index and then batches to the main index at low traffic times.
- Reranker is a re-rank model run over top-K retrieved candidates; retraining is separate. For freshness-sensitive flows we suggest hybrid: vector similarity for recall + a small neural reranker tuned on recent labels.

Prompt governance (summary):
- Versioning: use semantic prompt IDs: prompt_id:v{major}.{minor} (e.g., support_resolution:v1.2). Store a canonical prompt artifact in your prompt inventory (attached template).
- Injection mitigations: 1) system-level instruction firewall (strip/normalize user inputs), 2) intent classifier to gate high-risk prompts, 3) structured-output enforcement plus schema validation so the model cannot return free-form sensitive actions.
- Red team: recommend a quarterly red-team pass per high-risk flow (billing, PII handling). We'll provide an initial set of adversarial test cases and help run a joint session.

Open items we'll cover Wed: mapping your acceptance tests to SDK examples, a proposed SOW scope for a 6-week pilot (integration + 1 red-team run), and dates for procurement milestones.

Attachments to share before meeting: short SDK quickstart, integration diagram, prompt inventory template, draft SOW (we'll push the SOW tomorrow).

—Dev
